title: How to Be Less Useful: The Joy of Inefficiency
description: A delightful book about reclaiming pleasure in mid-life—a potent mix of self-help and memoir, from one of today’s wittiest, wisest voices. “A hilarious chillout manual for cool people who want to be more than their appointments and obligations.” —Samantha Irby "I have done everything right, and I have missed everything." Think about what we choose to cut out or overlook as we approach the deep end of adulthood: Dessert. Naps. Pretty underwear. Sweaty dancing. “Pointless” hangs with the people we love most. And then, activities that used to be fun somehow lose their luster, usually in the decade between thirty and forty: summer vacation (exhaustion), stay-in-touch texting (bandwidth), finding the perfect restaurant (the algorithm). When did our lives become entirely about efficiency and optimization? Priyanka Mattoo shares her journey toward being less useful, delivering life lessons without an ounce of preachiness or pressure. She looks at where pleasure begins and what it serves. Did you know karaoke can cure a stomachache? Or that Paddington Bear is a stealth lifestyle guru? Or that nobody actually asked you to do that labor-intensive thing you begrudgingly did? With self-deprecating humor, devastating insight, and bracing honesty, Priyanka shows us how to step out of the grind as a friend, as a partner, even as a parent, and welcome joy back into our lives without burning it all down. What if, instead of being useful, we could all learn how to be happier, lighter, more present, more engaged? title: How to Be Less Useless: An Adulting Guide for People Who Were Never Properly Taught Anythi
description: How to Be Less Useless An Adulting Guide for People Who Were Never Properly Taught Anything So... you're an adult now. Nobody gave you an instruction manual. Nobody explained why everything costs so much, how you're supposed to keep your house clean, what the hell a credit score actually is, or why the washing machine suddenly sounds like it's trying to escape. Don't worry. You're not the only one. How to Be Less Useless is a funny, practical guide to all the everyday stuff you're somehow expected to know as an adult. Inside, you'll learn how to: Stop being permanently skint Cook something other than toast Survive laundry without destroying your clothes Deal with bills before they become a problem Clean your home before it becomes a biological experiment Handle basic DIY without making things worse Understand credit scores and your bank account Know what to look for before signing contracts Deal with broken stuff without immediately panicking Have people over without pretending your house is a hotel This isn't a boring lecture about becoming a "better person." It's a guide to becoming slightly less useless . No perfection. No corporate bullshit. No pretending you've got your entire life figured out. Just practical advice, common sense, and a bit of humour for anyone who's ever thought: "Why the fuck did nobody teach me this?" Welcome to adulthood. You're probably going to be fine. title: Master the Art of the Excuse and Never Do Anything Useful: Scientifically Effective Excuse
description: Master the Art of the Excuse and Never Do Anything Useful What if your biggest obstacle isn't laziness, lack of talent, bad luck, or even fear? What if it's your ability to explain everything? In this darkly funny and brutally honest satirical guide, THE SOCIAL VULTURE dissects the world's most sophisticated excuses: "I'm not ready yet," "I need motivation," "I'll start tomorrow," "I'm waiting for clarity," and the countless elegant stories we tell ourselves while our lives remain stuck in the waiting room. Part psychological observation, part social satire, and part uncomfortable mirror, this book exposes how intelligent people sabotage themselves with explanations that sound wise, mature, and reasonable—but quietly keep them trapped. Inside, you'll discover: Why preparation often becomes procrastination in disguise. How fear learns to speak the language of wisdom. Why motivation is one of the least reliable forces in personal growth. How old wounds become lifelong alibis. Why waiting for the perfect moment may be the perfect way to waste your life. Practical tools to dismantle excuses without becoming ruthless toward yourself. Sharp, witty, and occasionally painful, Master the Art of the Excuse and Never Do Anything Useful is for anyone who suspects they may be standing in the way of their own potential. Because the most dangerous excuse isn't the one you know is a lie. It's the one that sounds true.  if(window.mix_csa){window.mix_csa('[cel_widget_id="tell-amazon-desktop_DetailPage_5"]', '#CardInstanceGKqHBBZE2PoBQ61574mXmQ')('mark', 'bb')} if(window.uet){window.uet('bb','tell-amazon-desktop_DetailPage_5',{wb: 1})} ._tell-amazon-desktop_style_tell_amazon_icon_core_report__Fs1ah{color:#0f1111;color:var(--aok-sfs-color-page-primary-normal-fg,#0f1111);display:inline-bloc

title: I Want To Be a Useless Person: A Guide to Living Fully by Doing Less
description: What if the most radical thing you could do was absolutely nothing? We live in a world that measures your worth by your output. Hustle harder. Do more. Sleep less. Be productive — or be forgotten. But what if the whole system is broken? I Want To Be a Useless Person is a quiet rebellion against the grind. Written with warmth, honesty, and a little humor, this book dismantles the myth that your value is tied to your productivity — and invites you to imagine a life that feels less like a race and more like home. Across 21 chapters, you will learn to: Unlearn the hustle gospel that has been sold to you since childhood Reclaim rest, boredom, and stillness as acts of courage — not laziness Rebuild your relationships, creativity, and sense of self outside of achievement Say no — to the grind, to guilt, and to a life you never actually chose This is not a book about giving up. It's a book about waking up. To slower mornings. Deeper connections. A version of yourself that doesn't need to earn the right to exist. You are not a machine. You never were.  if(window.mix_csa){window.mix_csa('[cel_widget_id="tell-amazon-desktop_DetailPage_2"]', '#CardInstancek6Lk1mTJWN8e6adjV-wjZA')('mark', 'bb')} if(window.uet){window.uet('bb','tell-amazon-desktop_DetailPage_2',{wb: 1})} ._tell-amazon-desktop_style_tell_amazon_icon_core_report__Fs1ah{color:#0f1111;color:var(--aok-sfs-color-page-primary-normal-fg,#0f1111);display:inline-block;-webkit-filter:none;filter:none;-webkit-filter:var(--aok-sfs-effect-mode-dark-color-silhouette-white,none);filter:var(--aok-sfs-effect-mode-dark-color-silhouette-white,none);height:20px;margin-right:4px;width:20px}._tell-amazon-desktop_style_tell_amazon_modal_spinner__3bz5K,._tell-amazon-desktop_style_tell_amazon_popover_inner__3tPIV{padding:20px 24px 0;width:65v

title: The Book of Not Entirely Useful Advice
description: From acclaimed writer A.F. Harrold comes a riotous poetry collection that encourages readers to think critically--perfect for fans of Shel Silverstein! Packed with silly rhymes and witty wordplay, A.F. Harrold's poetry is positively bursting with fun--and advice. But it's not always the most useful. . . Never apologize to a door you've walked into, unless it's a really special door. Don't serve a cat soup when the cat wants jelly. Tomato soup won't fill a feline belly. Don't put a rock in a roll, unless you hate having teeth. Among the seemingly nonsensical stanzas on onions, sausages, and kilted koalas are exercises in critical thinking--what advice should readers follow, and what should they dismiss? Harrold's short, clever poems work seamlessly alongside Mini Grey's vibrant art to create visual gags that will have readers in stitches. title: The Best Book About Nothing: 501 Gloriously Useless (and Completely True) Facts for Curiou
description: Congratulations. You are holding 501 facts you do not need — and a gift for the person who has everything. Give it as a white-elephant or stocking gift, leave it by the couch, or open it anywhere. Not one fact will fix your car, do your taxes or get you a raise. And yet, by the last page, you'll know why wombat poop comes out in cubes, what the dot over an i is called, and why every U.S. bill issued since 1861 is still good money. The Best Book About Nothing is a trivia book for grown-ups who love a good "wait, really?" Every fact is gloriously useless. Every fact is also true: each one was checked against two published sources from independent organizations, and every source is listed at the back, by fact number. Inside you'll find: 501 numbered facts in 20 themed chapters, from "Animals Accomplishing Nothing" and "Space Is Mostly Nothing" to "Presidents' Pointless Particulars" and "Patently Ridiculous," plus one bonus fact saved for the very end. "Nope, Not True" boxes that take down famous myths your uncle still repeats. A True/False quiz at the end of every chapter, with answers at the back that point to the fact that settles it. Sources for every fact , so you can win the argument at dinner. A few things you didn't need to know: During World War I, a flock of sheep grazed the White House lawn. A day on Venus is longer than its year. Octopuses have three hearts and blue blood. Read it front to back, open it anywhere, or leave it by the couch for when the conversation needs help. It makes an easy gift for the person who has everything: give them nothing. Every fact checked.
